extracted.intended_audience: poets, creative writers, and literary critics interested in poetic composition and criticism (particularly readers of Walt Whitman / Leaves of Grass)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for composing and judging poetry, especially a project aiming to represent American personality and experience; includes authorial statements about method, aims, materials, and readerly/critical criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heine's two principles of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: H. Heine's first principle: 'What motive is the author trying to carry out, or express or accomplish?' Second principle: 'Has he achiev'd it?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a work by discerning the author's intended motive and then judging whether the work successfully realizes that motive. These two questions are presented as primary, concise evaluative checkpoints for criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositional theory of Leaves of Grass (possession of the author's mind)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory: to thoroughly possess the mind, memory, cognizance of the author himself, with everything beforehand -- a full armory of concrete actualities, observations, humanity, past poems, ballads, facts, technique, war and peace, politics, North and South, East and West, nothing too large or too small, the sciences as far as possible -- and above all America and the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a poetical work by internalizing a very wide, concrete range of materials and knowledge; let this store inform the poem. The subject is then handed over to the author's Emotionality/Personality to be shaped. Expect the resulting work to bear the author's personal imprint and to display both strengths and faults arising from that personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn subject over to Emotionality / Personality
rubrics_metrics.description: After assembling concrete materials and knowledge, the subject of the poem is 'turned over to his Emotionality, even Personality, to be shaped thence; and emerges strictly therefrom, with all its merits and demerits on its head.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The shaping force should be the author's emotional and personal sensibility rather than an external, detached artifice; authenticity of voice is central even if it makes style unconventional or offensive to norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as expression of essential Religion (higher moral aim)
rubrics_metrics.description: In its highest aspect, essential Poetry expresses and goes along with essential Religion -- more serviceable to true religion than priests, creeds, and churches; as opposed to poetry that is merely ornamental, dainty, or a 'love-sigh.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value poetic work that carries moral, spiritual, or existential depth rather than merely decorative or fashionable effects. Aim for works that engage with enduring human conditions (illness, death, endurance) and have substantive ethical or religious resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid serving merely the amusement of the multitude (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unsatisfactory for an earnest spirit to serve merely the amusement of the multitude; mere ornament or intellectual finesse that caters only to low prevailing tastes is inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize superficial charm, cleverness, or popular trendiness over depth and seriousness. Resist making the work merely pleasing at the expense of its larger aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent the 'bulk average' of the people (subject-matter criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on the final average or bulk quality of the whole people; aim to give a fair reflection and representation of shows, questions, humanity, events, and unfoldings of one's age and nation (the American bulk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor poetic work in broad, democratic, and representative human experience rather than exclusively elite or esoteric concerns. The writer's claim to value is linked to how well the work derives from and returns to this 'bulk' of humanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete particulars and domestic/physical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman's compositional practice is grounded in tangible, domestic, and sensory particulars (e.g., detailed description of his room, books, objects, stove, arm-chair, photographs, proofs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground poems in vivid, specific, physical details to give authenticity and to connect larger themes to everyday reality. Concrete items and settings serve as an 'armory' of material for poetic invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study texts before performance to gain mastery (preparation for reception and understanding)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a young fellow the author 'always studied a play or libretto quite carefully over, (sometimes twice through) before seeing it on the stage' and found he gained most by mastering the text first if the piece had depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For understanding or interpreting dramatic/performative works (and by extension for composing works intended for performance), read and internalize the text before encountering a staging; preparation increases depth of appreciation and critical insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tonal and structural shifts to avoid monotony
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cluster 'Good-Bye my Fancy' Whitman 'changes the clef to its lowest' and the book is 'a lot of tremolos about old age, death, and faith' and is 'garrulous, irascible' with 'various breaks and even tricks to avoid monotony.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating somber or limited thematic ranges (old age, death, faith), employ tonal shifts, structural breaks, and formal devices to maintain variety and reader engagement. Expect such devices to complicate easy comprehension and to require readers/critics to 'cipher' the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept that style will often offend conventions if authentic
rubrics_metrics.description: Every page of Whitman's utterance 'smacks of the living physical identity, date, environment, individuality, probably beyond anything known, and in style often offensive to the conventions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize authentic voice and lived identity even when style violates established literary conventions; anticipate critical resistance but regard it as part of a candid, personal poetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be willing to revise and grow works over long periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaves of Grass underwent multiple stages of growth and hitches/splices over decades, with annexes and additions (e.g., 'Good-Bye my Fancy' as concluding annex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat major poetic projects as evolving works that may be expanded, revised, and reissued across years. Accept iterative development rather than expecting finished perfection at first publication.
